content: 1. It is essential to adhere to the prescribed schedule for taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your next dose at the regular time. 2. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. 3. Before taking ethambutol, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ethambutol may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Alcohol consumption may increase the risk of liver disease. 5. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, if you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to the infant. 6. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 7. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 8. While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as sputum tests, eye/vision exams, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts.
